demand.title: Demand
demand.introduction: You want more booked jobs, and your answers point at demand, the number of calls coming in. Before we talk about getting more, let us make sure the ones you already get are not slipping away, because that is usually the faster win. Here is the honest read.
demand.body: Your answers point at the top of the funnel, not enough calls coming in the door. I want to be straight with you here. If you are truly out of demand, more automation is not your first fix, and I would rather say that than sell you something. But demand is also the problem people name most often when the real issue is that the calls they do get are quietly slipping away. So before you spend a dollar getting found, it is worth making sure you are keeping what already comes in.
demand.plan: Start by counting. For two weeks, track how many calls, texts, and form fills you actually get, and how many turned into booked jobs. Most owners find the top of the funnel is fuller than it felt. If the calls are there and the jobs are not, the leak is after the call, and that is fixable fast. If the calls genuinely are not there, that is a marketing conversation, an honest one, not an automation one.

lead_response.title: Lead response
lead_response.introduction: You want more booked jobs, and the fastest path is not more leads, it is keeping the ones you already get. Your answers point at lead response as the biggest thing standing between you and a fuller schedule.
lead_response.body: This is the leak that quietly costs the most for almost every shop. A call comes in while you are on a job, driving, or under a sink, and it goes to voicemail. Most people do not leave one. They just call the next name on the list. You never see the job you lost, which is exactly why it is so easy to ignore. The shop that answers first, or even just texts back first, usually wins the work.
lead_response.plan: Put something between the missed call and the lost job. The simplest version is an automatic text that fires the second a call goes unanswered, in your voice, asking what they need and offering a time. It costs almost nothing and it turns calls you were already losing back into booked jobs. That one change is where I start with most businesses, because it pays for itself the fastest.

estimate_follow_up.title: Estimate follow up
estimate_follow_up.introduction: You want more booked jobs, and you are closer than it feels. Your answers point at estimate follow up, the quotes you already sent that went quiet. Those are booked jobs waiting to be claimed.
estimate_follow_up.body: You already did the hard part. You took the call, went out, and sent the quote. Then it went quiet, and most quotes that go quiet never get a second touch. That is a job you already earned, sitting on the table, waiting for someone to follow up. Usually nobody does, because everyone is busy doing the next job.
estimate_follow_up.plan: Give every quote a simple follow up sequence, so a silent quote gets a gentle second and third touch on its own instead of being forgotten. Nothing pushy, just a reminder that you are ready when they are. A few more points of close rate on quotes you already sent is found money, because you already paid to create them.

cash_flow.title: Cash flow
cash_flow.introduction: You want more booked jobs. Your answers point at cash flow, which sounds unrelated, but a shop starved for cash makes worse decisions about which work to chase. Steady the money and booking the right jobs gets easier.
cash_flow.body: The work is getting done, but the money comes in slow. Invoices go out late because someone has to remember to send them, then they sit unpaid because nobody is chasing. The job is finished in the field long before it is finished in the bank, and that gap is where cash flow quietly strangles a busy shop.
cash_flow.plan: Close the gap between finishing the job and getting paid. The fix is to have the invoice go out automatically the moment a job is marked done, with a polite reminder if it goes unpaid. You did the work. The goal is to get paid for it without anyone having to remember to ask.

owner_dependency.title: It mostly rests on you
owner_dependency.introduction: You want more booked jobs, but your answers show the business mostly runs through you. That is the real ceiling. More jobs will not help if every one of them still needs you in the room.
owner_dependency.body: Right now the business runs when you run it. The calls, the quotes, the follow ups, the decisions, they all move because you are in the room. That is not a knock on you, it is how almost every good shop starts. But it means your growth is capped at your own hours, and the day you want to step back, or have to, the whole thing slows down with you.
owner_dependency.plan: Take one thing off your plate that does not need your judgment, the most repetitive one. Usually that is the follow up, the reminders, the chasing, the stuff that only happens when you remember. Hand that first piece to a system that does it every time. You get hours back and you prove the business can run a step without you. Then you do the next piece.

past_customer_follow_up.title: Past customer follow up
past_customer_follow_up.introduction: You want more booked jobs, and the easiest ones are people who already hired you. Your answers point at past customer follow up, a list of ready buyers you are not reaching out to.
past_customer_follow_up.body: The cheapest job to win is one you already earned. Your past customers already know you, already trust you, and already paid you once. But once a job is done most shops never reach out again, so those customers drift, and when they need you next they google someone else. A list of happy past customers is money sitting in a drawer.
past_customer_follow_up.plan: Put your past customers back to work. A simple scheduled reach out, a maintenance reminder, a seasonal check, or just a note that you are still here, brings back people who were always going to buy from someone. Same spirit as asking for a review the day you finish the job, quiet, automatic, every time. It is the lowest cost work you will ever win.
